Management outlook of ~70% revenue growth in FY2028; consensus FY2027 revenue $411.65B (+91%) and FY2028 $692.21B (+68%), EPS $9.31 and $15.91
AWS to deploy an additional 2 million NVIDIA GPUs in 2027-2028, mainly for agentic and physical AI, plus 100,000 GPUs for U.S. government data centers

Trade policy: 25% U.S. import tariff on licensed H200 shipments not passed through; further export-rule changes possible
Supply: dependence on TSMC CoWoS capacity and HBM suppliers; inventory provisions of $1.6B in 1H FY2027; purchase obligations and credit support/guarantees for customers' buildouts

stocks.name: Cognex
stocks.role: Machine vision for factories and warehouses

profile.what: The leading machine-vision supplier for factory inspection and warehouse barcode reading. Its agreed purchase of RealSense, for about $500M, adds depth cameras for mobile robots and humanoids.
drivers: Logistics automation: 10 straight quarters of double-digit growth through Q2 2026, driven by large e-commerce customers; FY2026 logistics outlook raised to high-single-digit growth.
Semiconductor and electronics upcycle tied to AI infrastructure: both guided to double-digit growth in 2026; Greater China revenue +42% (constant currency) and Other Asia +14% in Q2 2026.

Restructuring-driven margins: adjusted gross margin 71.5% (+350 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin 32.2% in Q2 2026; FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of 29-31% vs a 20-30% through-cycle target; ~$35M of annualized cost savings by end-2026.
AI product cycle: OneVision generally available with hundreds of customers; In-Sight 2800/L38/3900/6900, SLX, and the In-Sight 1750 wafer reader (Sep 2026); ~9,000 new customers in 2025.
risks: Automotive weakness, especially in Europe: automotive revenue fell at a high-single-digit rate in Q2 2026 and Europe revenue fell 15%.
Logistics deceleration and customer concentration: management expects logistics growth to moderate in H2 2026, and one customer has at times been a material share of revenue.

High expectations: Q3 2025 included a $13M one-time benefit, which makes for a tough Q3 comparison; Q2 2026 revenue slightly missed consensus and the stock fell ~5%; shares trade at ~53x trailing and ~31x forward earnings.
Input costs: memory price inflation is a ~75 bps gross-margin headwind in Q3 2026.

events.text: Set the Q3 2026 report for Nov 4, 2026 after the close; consensus revenue ~$313M.

Analyst moves from late Sep to mid-Oct: Baird cut its target to $70 (Neutral), Truist cut to $74 (Hold), and Barclays raised to $85 (Overweight, ~Oct 13). Shares fell from $61.82 (Oct 12 close) to $53.99 (Oct 16). Stock: −12.7% over Oct 13-16; cause not identified in sources reviewed.
Launched the In-Sight 1750 wafer reader for semiconductor manufacturers. Stock: close $58.19 (−1.3%); not clearly attributable.

Agreed to acquire RealSense for ~$500M in cash plus a $56.5M cash retention plan and ~$50M of RSUs. RealSense projects $80-90M of 2026 revenue (>50% growth); close expected Q4 2026; framed as Cognex's entry into robotic perception and physical AI. Stock: +0.5% premarket to $62.31 (RTT/Nasdaq) but closed at $58.97, roughly −5% on the day.

Q2 2026: record revenue of $291M (+17%), slightly below ~$292-293M consensus; adjusted EPS $0.45 (vs $0.42 consensus); adjusted EBITDA margin 32.2%; FY2026 guide of $1.13-1.15B revenue and $1.64-1.68 adjusted EPS. Management flagged moderating logistics growth in H2 and a ~75 bps memory-cost headwind in Q3. Stock: −5.4% post-earnings (AllInvestView); about −9.8% over the following month (Zacks, Sep 4).

stocks.name: Hesai Group
stocks.role: Lidar for cars and robots, with US-China policy risk

profile.what: A Chinese lidar maker selling to carmakers, robotaxi fleets, lawn robots and humanoids. In 2025 volumes roughly tripled while average prices halved; in Q2 26 units rose 78% and revenue 22%.
drivers: Volume ramp: FY2026 guide of 3.0-3.5M lidars vs 1.62M in 2025 (+85% to +116%); Q3 2026 revenue guide +38% to +45% YoY.
Robotics lidar >500k units in 2026 (vs ~240k), led by robotic lawnmowers (exclusive 10M-unit Dreame/MOVA agreement) plus 50+ embodied-AI customers.

Rising content per vehicle: ~US$200 at L2, ~US$350 for entry L3 and US$500-1,000 for advanced multi-lidar setups. Wins include Mercedes-Benz L3 (Europe and China), VW China JVs, Great Wall ETX (SOP late 2026), Li Auto (4 lidars on L8/L9), Xiaomi overseas (SOP 2027), Changan and GAC Toyota.
Market share: 44% of China's long-range ADAS lidar market in June 2026 (Gasgoo, 17th straight month as leader); ~43% global ADAS lidar share (Yole).
risks: ASP deflation: blended ASP fell from ~US$530 (2024) to ~US$260 (2025), and Q4 2025 blended ASP was down ~51% YoY (Dolphin). Revenue growth (+22% in Q2 2026) lags unit growth (+78%).
Gross margin compression: 42.5% in Q2 2025 vs 40.1% in Q2 2026; FY2026 guided only 'near 40%'.
China auto exposure: 74% of H1 2026 revenue came from mainland China; the price war and slowing China car sales hit the stock in Oct 2026, when CATL's weak Q3 drove an ~8% intraday drop.

US policy: remains on the 1260H list pending remand; DoD procurement restrictions from mid-2027; possible US limits on Chinese robotics components, FCC rules and tariffs, with North America at ~18% of revenue.

events.text: China auto supply-chain selloff after CATL's weak Q3 profit growth; Hesai fell >8% intraday toward its 52-week low and closed $12.14 on Oct 22. A 6D full-color lidar was announced around Oct 22. Stock: −5.7% on Oct 21 and −8.0% on Oct 22; rebound +8.2% on Oct 23 and +4.3% on Oct 26 to $13.69.
Launched the Kosmo 3D World Data Engine (Oct 14) and a 3D spatial camera for physical AI. Stock: about −5% (MarketBeat headline); closes $13.94 (Oct 14) to $13.36 (Oct 15) to $12.42 (Oct 16).

Q2 2026: revenue RMB860.8M (+21.9%), GM 40.1%, GAAP net income RMB70.6M (+60%), 628k lidars (+78%); Q3 guide RMB1.10-1.15bn (+38-45%); SGI 2026 guide raised to RMB200-300M. Same day, the DC Circuit reversed the 1260H district-court ruling on due-process grounds and remanded; Hesai remains listed. Stock: −6.1% premarket on Aug 18 (Finviz); closed $17.11, then $17.77 on Aug 19 (+3.9%).
1-for-8 share subdivision and ADS ratio change (1 ADS = 8 Class B shares) took effect; ADS count unchanged.
Pentagon's updated 1260H list adds Alibaba, Baidu, BYD and Unitree (RoboSense, Nio, CALB and EVE earlier in 2026); Hesai stays on the list.

Post-IPO low: intraday RMB404.03, close RMB405.10 (still +169% vs the IPO price). Stock: −3.5% on the day; ~-63% from the RMB1,100 peak.

Reports said China curbed humanoid-robot IPOs after Unitree's volatile debut (Reuters/The Information); SCMP (~Sep 15) cited a 'US$30 billion stock wipe-off' spurring regulatory caution. Stock: close RMB513.93 (−1.9%); slid to RMB470.00 by Sep 14 (stockanalysis closes).

Hit a record low of RMB571 intraday, 48% below the peak and ~RMB200bn of value lost; rebounded to RMB615.03 on Aug 27. SCMP said the slump stoked fears of a humanoid bubble. Stock: −48% peak to trough in one week; +4.0% on Aug 27.

limits: Macro factors explain 20% to 60% of monthly moves for most of these stocks. Company news drives most of the rest, and the simulator cannot anticipate it.
Sensitivities change over time. The rolling chart shows real-yield sensitivity roughly doubling from 2019 to 2022 and fading since, so the long window and the recent window can disagree.

The fundamentals lens uses our own driver profiles, built from filings and stated assumptions. Elasticities and cost shares are estimates. The 80% ranges show how far the model's own estimates move when those inputs are uncertain; they leave out company news, so real outcomes spread wider.

The dollar, the factory cycle, tariffs, wages and the robotics forces come from the cash-flow model in both lenses, because history has no stable measure of them. Results for those forces rest on the driver profiles alone.

In scenarios that also move credit and the market a long way, such as the recession preset, the history lens can count part of the cycle twice: past spread blowouts came with downturns, so its credit and market betas already carry some of that damage.

Shocks are applied as if they happen at once, and their effects compound, so a 100bp cut lifts prices by more than a 100bp rise takes off. Very large moves, such as a 300bp rate shock, push the model past the range of its history.
Returns are in dollars, so currency moves are part of the returns of Japanese, Chinese and Hong Kong stocks. Per-share figures in the detail panel are in the listing currency.
Unitree listed on August 19, 2026, so its history lens is the peer average for Chinese growth names, with wide ranges.

Company inputs date from the October 27, 2026 research pass, which used October 26 closes. Teradyne reports after the close that day, Aurora on October 28 and Unitree by October 31, so their inputs may trail their newest results.
methodHtml:
History lens. Monthly dollar returns from January 2014 to October 2026 are regressed on the factors history measures reliably: the real 10-year yield, breakeven inflation, oil, copper, high-yield spreads, semiconductors against the market, China A-shares against the market and the part of the S&P 500 that macro does not explain. The three Japanese makers also carry the yen, measured net of the S&P 500. Short histories are pulled toward peer averages in proportion to their standard errors. A second window uses weekly returns since November 2023.

Fundamentals lens. Each company has a driver profile: revenue by end market, region and currency, cost shares for metals, magnets, chips, labor, energy and tariffed imports, pricing power, operating leverage, debt and cash. A twenty-year cash-flow model, with growth fading toward 3.5% and margins reaching their long-run level by year eight, is calibrated to today’s market value. The discount rate that reproduces the price is the company’s implied cost of capital, and the model’s sensitivity to it is the company’s duration. A scenario moves demand, costs, currency, funding and the value of future businesses through the cash flows, and moves the discount rate through that duration.

Forces history cannot measure. The dollar, the factory cycle, tariffs, wage growth, magnet supply, Chinese price competition, funding conditions, safety incidents and the humanoid timeline enter both lenses through the cash-flow model. Their measured betas are unstable or missing: dollar betas change sign depending on what else is in the regression, and survey-based activity indexes move after prices do. The two lenses therefore agree on these forces, and any gap between them comes from rates, credit, the market, oil, copper, chips, China and the yen.

Why rates move. A 10-year move is split into real yield and breakeven inflation according to its cause. Growth-led rises also lift expected cash flows and come with tighter credit and firmer activity, so the same 100bp does far less damage than a rise driven by term premium or Fed tightening. Inflation-led rises pass partly into nominal growth, by as much as each company can pass costs on.

Blend and ranges. The headline blends both lenses, equal-weighted by default. Each run draws 320 versions of the uncertain inputs: beta standard errors, demand elasticities, cost pass-through, operating leverage, duration, the risk-premium response, currency effects, price-war intensity, funding terms and the value of future businesses, shared across companies so the basket keeps their correlation. The 80% range is the spread of those model estimates. It leaves out company news, so actual outcomes spread wider. A rate move brings the dollar and yen moves that history pairs with it. Oil, copper, credit and the cycle follow the cause you pick, because their link to rates flips sign depending on why rates moved.
refreshNote: Prices and macro series run to the October 26, 2026 close and refresh each weekday after the US close through a scheduled workflow that pulls Yahoo Finance and FRED and re-estimates every sensitivity. Company profiles date from the October 27, 2026 research pass; market values follow the latest prices.
